title_en: Top Trump Officials Are Hitting the Campaign Trail Ahead of the Midterms. Are They Allowed To?
excerpt_en: Legal experts and advocacy groups contend that in seeking to boost Republicans ahead of the midterms, members of the Administration have violated a decades-old law.

enrich.title_zh: 特朗普政府高层频频下场助选中期选举，这样做合法吗？
enrich.summary_zh: 美国中期选举临近，特朗普政府多位高层官员频繁出席竞选活动，为共和党人站台拉票。法律专家和倡议团体认为，这些官员谋求为共和党助选的做法，违反了美国沿用数十年的一部法律。文章由此追问：行政官员参与党派竞选活动到底是否合法，界限又在哪里。

paragraphs.en: Legal experts and advocacy groups contend that in seeking to boost Republicans ahead of the midterms, members of the Administration have violated a decades-old law.
paragraphs.zh: 法律专家和倡议团体认为，政府成员在中期选举前为共和党人拉抬声势的举动，已经违反了一部沿用数十年的法律。

vocab.meaning_zh: 主张、坚称（常用于法律或争论语境，表示一方提出的有争议的说法，而非已被证实的事实）
vocab.example_en: Critics contend that the new rule unfairly targets small businesses.
vocab.example_zh: 批评者主张，新规不公平地针对了小企业。

vocab.meaning_zh: 倡议团体、游说组织（致力于推动某一公共议题或监督政府行为的非营利组织）
vocab.example_en: An advocacy group filed a complaint with the oversight office.
vocab.example_zh: 一家倡议团体向监督机构提交了投诉。

vocab.meaning_zh: 提振、拉抬（此处指为候选人或政党造势、增加其胜选机会）
vocab.example_en: The rally was intended to boost turnout among young voters.
vocab.example_zh: 这场集会旨在提高年轻选民的投票率。

vocab.meaning_zh: 在……之前、临近……之时（外刊常用来表达“某事件到来前夕”）
vocab.example_en: The report was released ahead of the summit.
vocab.example_zh: 这份报告在峰会前夕发布。

vocab.meaning_zh: 中期选举（美国总统任期中途举行的国会及州级选举，美国政治的固定说法）
vocab.example_en: Historically, the president's party loses seats in the midterms.
vocab.example_zh: 从历史上看，总统所属政党往往会在中期选举中丢掉席位。

vocab.meaning_zh: 已有数十年历史的、沿用数十年的（新闻体中常用来暗示某项法规“陈旧但仍在生效”）
vocab.example_en: They are challenging a decades-old zoning rule.
vocab.example_zh: 他们正在挑战一条沿用数十年的分区法规。

sentences.en: Legal experts and advocacy groups contend that in seeking to boost Republicans ahead of the midterms, members of the Administration have violated a decades-old law.
sentences.structure: 主干：Legal experts and advocacy groups（主语）contend（谓语）that…（宾语从句）。从句主干：members of the Administration（主语）have violated（谓语）a decades-old law（宾语）；从句首的 in seeking to boost Republicans ahead of the midterms 是介词短语作状语，修饰 violated，交代“在何种行为中”违法。
sentences.analysis_zh: 这是一个“主语＋reporting verb＋that 从句”的典型新闻句式，用来把有争议的指控“挂”在消息来源名下，而不等于编辑部自己的判断——contend 而非 say，本身就带有“尚存争议”的色彩。从句把时间状语 in seeking to boost Republicans ahead of the midterms 提到句首，让“为共和党助选”这个行为先入眼，再落到“违反了某部老法律”的结论上，逻辑因果一目了然。注意 seeking to 表示“力图、谋求”，暗示检方关注的是意图；a decades-old law 不点明具体法名，是典型的悬念式写法，正文才展开。翻译时把介词短语提前处理成“……的举动”，比直译更符合中文语序。

background.title: “数十年之久的那部法律”通常指什么
background.text_zh: 在美国政治语境中，涉及“联邦行政官员能不能参与党派竞选活动”的老法律，最常被提及的是 1939 年通过的《哈奇法》（Hatch Act）。它限制联邦行政部门雇员利用公务身份和职权参与党派政治活动，包括筹款、助选和拉票，由联邦特别检察官办公室（OSC）负责监督，违规可能面临停职、降职甚至解职。需要说明的是，这只是一般的制度背景，给出的摘要原文并未点名任何具体法律。

background.title: 中期选举与“竞选行程”
background.text_zh: 中期选举（midterms）指总统四年任期中途举行的国会选举，众议院全部席位和约三分之一参议院席位改选，州长与地方职位也常同期举行，通常在选举年 11 月投票。选前数月，政治人物密集赴关键州演讲、筹款、为同党候选人站台，这种活动被形象地称为 “hitting the campaign trail”（踏上竞选行程）。争议焦点在于：总统本人和副总统作为民选官员享有较大的政治活动空间，而其他行政部门官员受的限制更严，因此“谁去站台、以什么身份站台”就成了法律问题。

title_en: Why Doctors Are Last to Know What’s in the Drug Supply
excerpt_en: The FDA should create an expedited pathway for clinical tests targeting emerging drug threats, write Dr. Shravani Durbhakula and Jeremy Kourvelas.

enrich.title_zh: 为什么医生总是最后才知道药品供应里有什么
enrich.summary_zh: 这段 RSS 提要只给出一句作者观点：FDA 应当为针对“新型药物威胁”的临床检测设立一条加急审批通道。提要由 Shravani Durbhakula 医生与 Jeremy Kourvelas 提出，并未展开论证细节。结合标题可以看出，文章关注的核心问题是：一线医生对药品供应链中实际流通的成分往往知情滞后，而监管层面的检测与审批速度跟不上新型药物威胁的出现速度。

paragraphs.en: The FDA should create an expedited pathway for clinical tests targeting emerging drug threats, write Dr. Shravani Durbhakula and Jeremy Kourvelas.
paragraphs.zh: Shravani Durbhakula 医生与 Jeremy Kourvelas 写道，FDA 应当为针对新型药物威胁的临床检测开辟一条加急通道。

vocab.meaning_zh: 加急的、快速办理的；在监管语境中指比常规流程更快获批或处理
vocab.example_en: The agency set up an expedited review process for the new test.
vocab.example_zh: 该机构为这项新检测设立了加急审评流程。

vocab.meaning_zh: 路径、通道；在药品与医疗器械监管中是固定术语，指某类产品获得批准或上市所走的程序渠道
vocab.example_en: There is still no clear regulatory pathway for this kind of device.
vocab.example_zh: 这类器械目前仍没有明确的监管审批通道。

vocab.meaning_zh: 临床检测、临床试验性检验；指在人体样本或患者身上进行的检验，而非实验室里的基础研究
vocab.example_en: The clinical tests can identify the substance within hours.
vocab.example_zh: 这些临床检测能在数小时内识别出该物质。

vocab.meaning_zh: 针对、以……为对象（此处为分词形式 targeting，修饰 clinical tests）
vocab.example_en: The new rules target products sold online.
vocab.example_zh: 新规针对的是线上销售的产品。

vocab.meaning_zh: 新出现的、正在浮现的；外刊常用来形容尚未被充分认识、但已开始造成影响的风险或威胁
vocab.example_en: Public health officials are tracking an emerging threat.
vocab.example_zh: 公共卫生官员正在追踪一种新出现的威胁。

vocab.meaning_zh: 药品供应（链）；在美式语境中也常指非法药物的流通渠道与货源
vocab.example_en: Doctors rarely know what is actually in the drug supply.
vocab.example_zh: 医生很少知道药品供应里究竟是什么成分。

sentences.en: The FDA should create an expedited pathway for clinical tests targeting emerging drug threats, write Dr. Shravani Durbhakula and Jeremy Kourvelas.
sentences.structure: 主干：The FDA should create an expedited pathway（主语 The FDA + 情态动词 should + 谓语 create + 宾语 an expedited pathway）。修饰：for clinical tests 是介词短语，作 pathway 的后置定语，说明这条通道是给什么用的；targeting emerging drug threats 是现在分词短语，作 clinical tests 的后置定语，说明检测针对的是什么；句末 write Dr. Shravani Durbhakula and Jeremy Kourvelas 是引述动词加主语的倒装结构，交代说话人。
sentences.analysis_zh: 这句是新闻写作中典型的“引语前置”句式：把说话人的观点放在前面，把 write / said 加作者放在句末，好处是让观点本身占据句首最重要的位置，读者先看到主张，再看是谁说的。理解时要先把主干 The FDA should create a pathway 抓住，再一层层往右挂修饰：什么样的 pathway（加急的）→ 给谁的（给临床检测的）→ 哪种检测（针对新型药物威胁的）。注意主句用了 should，语气是“提出建议”，而不是陈述已经发生的事实，因此译文用“应当”而非“将会”。

background.title: FDA 与“加急通道”
background.text_zh: FDA（美国食品药品监督管理局）负责审批药品、疫苗、医疗器械和体外诊断检测。常规审批耗时较长，因此 FDA 设有多种加速机制，例如针对严重疾病的 Fast Track（快速通道）、Breakthrough Therapy（突破性疗法认定）、Accelerated Approval（加速批准）以及针对公共卫生紧急情况的 Emergency Use Authorization（紧急使用授权）。提要中说的 expedited pathway，就是要求为某类特定产品再开一条类似的高优先级审评入口，从而缩短检测工具从研发到可用之间的时间。

background.title: “drug supply”的两层含义
background.text_zh: 在英文媒体里，drug supply 可以指合法的药品供应链，也可以指非法药物的流通货源。标题说医生“最后才知道”里面有什么，正是这两种语境的交叉点：合法药品有成分说明书，但非法市场上流通的物质往往成分不明、掺杂掺假。近年美国公共卫生领域高度关注非法药物供应中掺杂芬太尼（fentanyl）以及兽用镇静剂赛拉嗪（xylazine，俗称“tranq”）等新型成分，因为这些成分不在常规毒品筛查面板里，临床上一时难以检出，医生常常是在患者出现异常症状之后才反推。以上为背景知识，提要本身并未展开这些内容。

title_en: Tusk defends overhaul of Poland’s constitutional court despite protests
excerpt_en: Prime minister says shake-up is vital to restore tribunal crippled by years of political disputes
body_en: Poland’s prime minister, Donald Tusk, has vowed to see through a contested overhaul of the country’s constitutional court, declaring that “in certain matters, there can be no compromise”.

In a prime-time television address on Saturday night, Tusk was defiant, despite overnight protests that saw riot police drafted to protect the court’s building, saying the shake-up was vital to restore a tribunal crippled by years of political disputes.
Related: Riot police deployed to Poland’s constitutional court after judge suspended
Paralysed for more than a decade, the court sat at the core of rule of law clashes between the rightwing Law and Justice (PiS) party and the EU during the party’s eight-year rule.

Since returning to office in 2023, the centre-right Tusk has sought to unwind those judicial changes, but his agenda has been frustrated by opposition-aligned presidents with extensive veto powers. Earlier this year, president Karol Nawrocki refused to swear in five judges approved by parliament.

The crisis flared again on Friday when a group of government-backed judges attempted to seize procedural control of the tribunal, suspending the PiS-appointed chief judge and deputy and prompting street protests.
Defending the action, Tusk said “there was never any doubt that the court in the form imposed by PiS was not a genuine court”, citing adverse rulings from European tribunals.
He compared the opposition outrage to “a thief snatching an elderly woman’s handbag, running off, and when he is caught, he screams that he is subjected to violence”.

Tusk said: “Let’s call things for what they are: for years, there have been organisations and politicians in Poland who seek to destroy democracy and the rule of law. It is no coincidence they find support among pro-Russian forces globally.”

He later highlighted that Russia’s former president Dmitry Medvedev had joined the opposition in an outcry over the changes, accusing Warsaw of “a constitutional coup” and “hounding the conservatives”. “And everything is clear,” Tusk said.

He also criticised opposition-aligned Nawrocki for joining the protests on Friday night and forcing his entry into the court’s building to intervene. “In a democratic state, no politician can enter a court to issue orders or intimidate judges – not even the president,” Tusk said. “We Poles have succeeded too well in building a strong state to surrender now.”
He said it was the government’s duty to ensure its security and the conditions necessary for the court to operate. “And I intend to fulfil that duty,” he said.
On Saturday, the European Commission urged Nawrocki to approve the new judges who were nominated by parliament, so the court could function in line with the constitution and EU law.
A spokesperson for the commission said its executive was “following closely” the events in Poland.

“It is for the Polish authorities to ensure that the constitutional tribunal can function in accordance with the Polish constitution and in respect of the relevant case law of the court of justice of the European Union,” the spokesperson said, appearing to ally the bloc with the Polish government.

However, the spokesperson also highlighted that the European court of human rights issued an interim finding in May that obliged Polish authorities to “refrain from hindering the taking up and exercise of judicial duties” by judges who are still waiting to be sworn in.
The confrontation sets the battle lines before next year’s parliamentary election, with polls pointing to a close race between Tusk’s broad coalition and the nationalist right.
However, experts remain divided over whether the government’s procedural gambit at the court is lawful.
Poland’s Helsinki Foundation for Human Rights said on Saturday the legal basis for the temporary suspension was “questionable”, warning it would “not contribute” to restoring the court.

The foreign minister, Radosław Sikorski, conceded that the events outside the court were “not elegant”, but insisted: “The alternative was to concede an unconstitutional transformation of Poland into a presidential republic.”

Nawrocki held some cross-party political talks on Saturday, with no apparent breakthrough. His senior aide, Zbigniew Bogucki, responded to Tusk’s address, calling the prime minister “a pathological liar, who is setting Poland ablaze”.

enrich.title_zh: 图斯克为波兰宪法法庭改革辩护，抗议声中坚持推进
enrich.summary_zh: 波兰总理图斯克发表电视讲话，坚持推进对宪法法庭的改组。此前政府支持的法官将PiS任命的首席法官停职，引发街头抗议和防暴警察进驻法院。图斯克称该法庭早已被政治纷争弄得瘫痪、并非真正的法院，并把反对派的指责斥为贼喊捉贼。欧盟委员会敦促总统批准新法官，但也提醒欧洲人权法院的临时裁定；专家对政府此举是否合法仍有分歧。

paragraphs.en: Poland’s prime minister, Donald Tusk, has vowed to see through a contested overhaul of the country’s constitutional court, declaring that “in certain matters, there can be no compromise”.
paragraphs.zh: 波兰总理唐纳德·图斯克誓言要将他备受争议的宪法法庭改革推行到底，并宣称“在某些问题上，不存在妥协的余地”。

paragraphs.en: In a prime-time television address on Saturday night, Tusk was defiant, despite overnight protests that saw riot police drafted to protect the court’s building, saying the shake-up was vital to restore a tribunal crippled by years of political disputes.
paragraphs.zh: 在周六晚间的电视黄金时段讲话中，图斯克态度强硬。前一晚的抗议迫使防暴警察被调来守卫法院大楼，但他仍表示，这场改组对于重振一个被多年政治纷争弄得瘫痪的法庭至关重要。

paragraphs.en: Related: Riot police deployed to Poland’s constitutional court after judge suspended
paragraphs.zh: 相关报道：法官被停职后，防暴警察进驻波兰宪法法庭

paragraphs.en: Paralysed for more than a decade, the court sat at the core of rule of law clashes between the rightwing Law and Justice (PiS) party and the EU during the party’s eight-year rule.
paragraphs.zh: 该法庭瘫痪已十余年。在右翼法律与公正党（PiS）执政的八年间，它一直处于该党与欧盟之间法治冲突的核心。

paragraphs.en: Since returning to office in 2023, the centre-right Tusk has sought to unwind those judicial changes, but his agenda has been frustrated by opposition-aligned presidents with extensive veto powers. Earlier this year, president Karol Nawrocki refused to swear in five judges approved by parliament.
paragraphs.zh: 自2023年重新执政以来，中右翼的图斯克一直试图撤销这些司法改动，但他的议程屡屡被与反对派结盟、握有广泛否决权的总统所挫败。今年早些时候，总统卡罗尔·纳夫罗茨基拒绝为议会批准的五名法官主持宣誓就职。

paragraphs.en: The crisis flared again on Friday when a group of government-backed judges attempted to seize procedural control of the tribunal, suspending the PiS-appointed chief judge and deputy and prompting street protests.
paragraphs.zh: 周五，危机再度爆发：一群获得政府支持的法官试图夺取该法庭的程序控制权，将PiS任命的首席法官和副庭长停职，并由此引发街头抗议。

paragraphs.en: Defending the action, Tusk said “there was never any doubt that the court in the form imposed by PiS was not a genuine court”, citing adverse rulings from European tribunals.
paragraphs.zh: 图斯克为该行动辩护，援引欧洲各法庭作出的不利裁决，称“从来没有人怀疑，PiS强加的那种形态的法院并不是一个真正的法院”。

paragraphs.en: He compared the opposition outrage to “a thief snatching an elderly woman’s handbag, running off, and when he is caught, he screams that he is subjected to violence”.
paragraphs.zh: 他把反对派的愤怒比作“一个小偷抢了老妇人的手袋，拔腿就跑，被抓到后却大喊自己遭到了暴力对待”。

paragraphs.en: Tusk said: “Let’s call things for what they are: for years, there have been organisations and politicians in Poland who seek to destroy democracy and the rule of law. It is no coincidence they find support among pro-Russian forces globally.”
paragraphs.zh: 图斯克说：“我们实话实说：多年来，波兰一直有一些组织和政客企图摧毁民主与法治。他们在全球亲俄势力当中获得支持，绝非巧合。”

paragraphs.en: He later highlighted that Russia’s former president Dmitry Medvedev had joined the opposition in an outcry over the changes, accusing Warsaw of “a constitutional coup” and “hounding the conservatives”. “And everything is clear,” Tusk said.
paragraphs.zh: 他随后强调，俄罗斯前总统德米特里·梅德韦杰夫也加入了反对派对这些改革的声讨，指责华沙搞“宪法政变”、“迫害保守派”。“这下一切都清楚了，”图斯克说。

paragraphs.en: He also criticised opposition-aligned Nawrocki for joining the protests on Friday night and forcing his entry into the court’s building to intervene. “In a democratic state, no politician can enter a court to issue orders or intimidate judges – not even the president,” Tusk said. “We Poles have succeeded too well in building a strong state to surrender now.”
paragraphs.zh: 他还批评与反对派结盟的纳夫罗茨基周五晚参加抗议，并强行进入法院大楼进行干预。“在一个民主国家，任何政客都不能进入法院发号施令或恐吓法官——即便是总统也不行，”图斯克说。“我们波兰人在建设一个强大国家方面成就卓著，绝不可能在此时放弃。”

paragraphs.en: He said it was the government’s duty to ensure its security and the conditions necessary for the court to operate. “And I intend to fulfil that duty,” he said.
paragraphs.zh: 他说，保障法院的安全以及法院运作所需的条件，是政府的职责。“我打算履行这一职责，”他说。

paragraphs.en: On Saturday, the European Commission urged Nawrocki to approve the new judges who were nominated by parliament, so the court could function in line with the constitution and EU law.
paragraphs.zh: 周六，欧盟委员会敦促纳夫罗茨基批准议会提名的这批新法官，以便该法庭能够依照宪法和欧盟法律运作。

paragraphs.en: A spokesperson for the commission said its executive was “following closely” the events in Poland.
paragraphs.zh: 欧盟委员会的一位发言人表示，该委员会的行政部门正在“密切关注”波兰的事态。

paragraphs.en: “It is for the Polish authorities to ensure that the constitutional tribunal can function in accordance with the Polish constitution and in respect of the relevant case law of the court of justice of the European Union,” the spokesperson said, appearing to ally the bloc with the Polish government.
paragraphs.zh: “确保宪法法庭能够依照波兰宪法、并遵照欧盟法院的相关判例法运作，是波兰当局的责任，”这位发言人说。这一表态似乎让欧盟站到了波兰政府一边。

paragraphs.en: However, the spokesperson also highlighted that the European court of human rights issued an interim finding in May that obliged Polish authorities to “refrain from hindering the taking up and exercise of judicial duties” by judges who are still waiting to be sworn in.
paragraphs.zh: 不过，这位发言人也强调，欧洲人权法院今年五月作出的一项临时裁定要求波兰当局“不得妨碍”那些仍在等待宣誓就职的法官“就任和履行司法职责”。

paragraphs.en: The confrontation sets the battle lines before next year’s parliamentary election, with polls pointing to a close race between Tusk’s broad coalition and the nationalist right.
paragraphs.zh: 这场对抗为明年的议会选举划定了战线。民调显示，图斯克的广泛联盟与民族主义右翼之间的竞争将十分胶着。

paragraphs.en: However, experts remain divided over whether the government’s procedural gambit at the court is lawful.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，对于政府在该法庭采取的程序性手段是否合法，专家们仍然意见不一。

paragraphs.en: Poland’s Helsinki Foundation for Human Rights said on Saturday the legal basis for the temporary suspension was “questionable”, warning it would “not contribute” to restoring the court.
paragraphs.zh: 波兰赫尔辛基人权基金会周六表示，此次临时停职的法律依据“值得质疑”，并警告此举“无助于”恢复该法庭。

paragraphs.en: The foreign minister, Radosław Sikorski, conceded that the events outside the court were “not elegant”, but insisted: “The alternative was to concede an unconstitutional transformation of Poland into a presidential republic.”
paragraphs.zh: 外交部长拉多斯瓦夫·西科尔斯基承认法院外发生的事件“不够体面”，但坚称：“另一种选择，就是听任波兰违宪地变成一个总统制共和国。”

paragraphs.en: Nawrocki held some cross-party political talks on Saturday, with no apparent breakthrough. His senior aide, Zbigniew Bogucki, responded to Tusk’s address, calling the prime minister “a pathological liar, who is setting Poland ablaze”.
paragraphs.zh: 纳夫罗茨基周六举行了一些跨党派政治会谈，但没有明显突破。他的高级助手兹比格涅夫·博古茨基回应图斯克的讲话，称总理是“一个病态的说谎者，正在把波兰点燃”。

vocab.meaning_zh: 把（困难的事）坚持到底、贯彻完成；此处不是“看穿”
vocab.example_en: The government promised to see through the reform despite fierce criticism.
vocab.example_zh: 尽管批评激烈，政府仍承诺将这项改革进行到底。

vocab.meaning_zh: （制度、机构的）全面改革、大修
vocab.example_en: The party promised a complete overhaul of the tax system.
vocab.example_zh: 该党承诺对税收制度进行全面改革。

vocab.meaning_zh: 公然不从的、强硬对抗的（形容明知有压力仍不退缩）
vocab.example_en: She remained defiant in the face of widespread criticism.
vocab.example_zh: 面对铺天盖地的批评，她依然不肯退让。

vocab.meaning_zh: （审理特定争议的）法庭、裁判所；文中指宪法法庭
vocab.example_en: The case was referred to an international tribunal.
vocab.example_zh: 该案被提交给一个国际法庭审理。

vocab.meaning_zh: 逐步撤销、回退（已推行的政策或改动）；此处不是“放松”
vocab.example_en: The new government began to unwind its predecessor’s reforms.
vocab.example_zh: 新政府开始逐步撤销前任的改革措施。

vocab.meaning_zh: （冲突、危机）骤然爆发、再度升级
vocab.example_en: Violence flared again in the border region last night.
vocab.example_zh: 昨晚边境地区的暴力事件再度爆发。

vocab.meaning_zh: （为取得优势而走的）一招、策略性举动，常含冒险意味
vocab.example_en: The procedural gambit may backfire on the government.
vocab.example_zh: 这一程序上的招数可能会反噬政府。

vocab.meaning_zh: （公众的）强烈抗议、哗然
vocab.example_en: The decision provoked a public outcry.
vocab.example_zh: 这一决定引发了公众的强烈抗议。

vocab.meaning_zh: （不断）追逼、纠缠、迫害
vocab.example_en: Critics say the media hounded him out of office.
vocab.example_zh: 批评者说媒体把他逼下了台。

vocab.meaning_zh: （不情愿地）承认
vocab.example_en: He conceded that mistakes had been made.
vocab.example_zh: 他承认出现了失误。

sentences.en: In a prime-time television address on Saturday night, Tusk was defiant, despite overnight protests that saw riot police drafted to protect the court’s building, saying the shake-up was vital to restore a tribunal crippled by years of political disputes.
sentences.structure: 主干：Tusk was defiant（主系表）。修饰：句首 In a prime-time television address... 为状语；despite overnight protests 为让步状语，其后 that saw riot police drafted to protect... 是定语从句修饰 protests（see 此处意为“见证、发生”，drafted 为过去分词作宾补）；句末 saying the shake-up was vital... 为现在分词作伴随状语，其中 crippled by years of political disputes 为过去分词短语后置修饰 a tribunal。
sentences.analysis_zh: 这句是典型的外刊“一句话交代全部要素”写法：先抛时间地点场景（黄金时段电视讲话），再给主句态度（defiant），用一个 despite 从句补上对立事实（抗议、防暴警察），最后用 saying 引出核心论点。翻译时可把 despite 从句提前，符合中文“先让步后转折”的顺序。注意 see 的用法：that saw riot police drafted 意为“（抗议中）出现了防暴警察被调派的情况”，不能译成“看到”。

sentences.en: Since returning to office in 2023, the centre-right Tusk has sought to unwind those judicial changes, but his agenda has been frustrated by opposition-aligned presidents with extensive veto powers.
sentences.structure: 并列复合句：前半主干 Tusk has sought to unwind those judicial changes（since returning... 为时间状语，returning 的逻辑主语与主句一致）；but 引出后半主干 his agenda has been frustrated by opposition-aligned presidents，with extensive veto powers 为介词短语后置修饰 presidents。
sentences.analysis_zh: 两个分句都是现在完成时，一句写“想做什么”，一句写“被什么挡住”，形成对照。opposition-aligned 是外刊高频复合形容词“与反对派结盟的”；presidents 用复数，是因为这一阻碍跨越多任总统。翻译时“frustrated”宜处理成“屡屡受挫、被挫败”，而不是简单的“使沮丧”。

sentences.en: However, the spokesperson also highlighted that the European court of human rights issued an interim finding in May that obliged Polish authorities to “refrain from hindering the taking up and exercise of judicial duties” by judges who are still waiting to be sworn in.
sentences.structure: 主干：the spokesperson highlighted that...（宾语从句）。宾语从句主干：the European court of human rights issued an interim finding；in May 为时间状语；that obliged Polish authorities to refrain from... 为定语从句修饰 an interim finding；refrain from 后接动名词短语 the taking up and exercise of judicial duties，by judges 引出动作主体；who are still waiting to be sworn in 为定语从句修饰 judges。
sentences.analysis_zh: 句子层层套叠：一个 that 引导宾语从句，从句里又有一个 that 定语从句，再套一个 who 定语从句。理解时先剥到最里层——欧洲人权法院五月作了临时裁定，裁定要求波兰当局不得妨碍某些法官履职，这些法官至今仍未被主持宣誓。作者把这一句放在欧盟委员会“似乎支持波兰政府”之后用 However 引出，是为了说明欧盟的态度其实两边都敲了一下，并非无条件站队。

background.title: 波兰宪法法庭与2015年以来的司法之争
background.text_zh: 宪法法庭（Trybunał Konstytucyjny）是波兰审查法律是否违宪的最高司法机构。2015年法律与公正党（PiS）上台后，围绕法官任命程序、法庭组成与裁决效力推行了一系列司法改革，被欧盟委员会指为破坏司法独立，并触发《欧盟条约》第7条程序，相关争议也多次诉至欧盟法院（CJEU）。图斯克2023年底联合政府上台后承诺“恢复法治”，但改革推进受阻于总统否决权与机构人事僵局，宪法法庭长期处于半瘫痪状态。

background.title: 波兰的总统否决权与“共治”格局
background.text_zh: 波兰是议会制与总统制混合的体制，总统由直选产生，对议会法案拥有否决权，议会需五分之三多数才能推翻，因此总统即便与政府不同阵营也能有效阻断立法。2023年议会选举后，图斯克的执政联盟与总统职位分属对立阵营，形成“共治”（cohabitation）；2025年卡罗尔·纳夫罗茨基当选总统后，这一对峙延续。文中提到的欧盟委员会、欧盟法院（CJEU）与欧洲人权法院（ECHR）分属不同体系：前者是欧盟机构，后两者分别是欧盟法院和欧洲委员会（非欧盟）下属的人权法院，不可混为一谈。

title_en: Fashion and tradition: how John Smedley is innovating in a tough market
excerpt_en: In the final article in a series on high-end British manufacturing we look at a clothing brand that dates to the 18th century but is increasingly on-trend
body_en: Tina is wielding a large pair of scissors with authority, slicing with immense skill and precision.

With 38 years of experience, she is an important member of the 230-strong manufacturing team producing fine knitwear for the John Smedley brand. Using a chalk, a semi-circular guide and a sharp pair of scissors, she cuts necklines in the knitted garments ready for the final trim to be attached.

The brand’s site in the Peak District, Derbyshire, is the oldest continuously operating factory in the world, with a maze of buildings, one of which dates to 1784. Inside is a mix of hi-tech Japanese knitting technology, skilled artisans such as Tina, who finish garments by hand, and some machines which date back more than 60 years and have to be kept going with bespoke parts. Another smaller Smedley factory, in Armthorpe, South Yorkshire, also finishes the garments.

The company – which holds royal warrants from King Charles and Queen Camilla – has faced difficult times in the luxury market in recent years, but is surviving by mixing heritage with innovation: from launching new designs and forging celebrity partnerships to investing in the latest equipment.
Most UK fashion manufacturing closed down more than 30 years ago as brands moved to cheaper offshore manufacturing locations such as China, India and Bangladesh.

There are 3,515 manufacturers of clothing in the UK, according to figures from the Office for National Statistics collated by UKFT, 315 fewer than a decade before. The number of people working in the industry is now just 15,000 according to the ONS, compared with 173,000 30 years ago.

Smedley has stayed true to its roots. It not only knits and puts together garments, but dyes cotton yarn, and washes, steams and packs the finished products, all in a beautiful wooded valley in Lea Bridge, near Matlock.
Water comes from a brook that runs under the factory with much of the steam for its processes generated by ancient-looking boilers as well as some shiny new silver ones.
Together, the workers produce 4,500 items a week not only under the John Smedley name, but under contract for high-end brands including Lanvin, Margaret Howell and Daks.
In 2024, it invested more than £4m in updating machinery to become more efficient and increase the range of styles it can make.

Jess McGuire-Dudley, the 41-year-old marketing expert who stepped up to be managing director last year after a decade at the company, says the family owners are “open to change”. “As long as it is in an appropriate way, that’s always embraced,” she says.

While some of its methods may be age-old, she says Smedley is increasingly on trend. The company is not struggling to attract new workers as, McGuire-Dudley says, young people are interested in craft skills and the sustainability aspect of making goods closer to home.
To help attract and retain people, the company has refurbished housing on its site to offer cheap accommodation alongside other staff benefits including pilates classes and a running club.
However, McGuire-Dudley says the factory is racing to train its younger workers as its most skilled employees near retirement age. The apprenticeship can take up to two years.
The commitment to craft skills is part of the founding philosophy that has protected John Smedley when other British-made brands have fallen away.
“He always had a vision of the highest quality produced for the top end of the market,” she says. “That is what we have tried to stay true to.”
The battle for survival is also self-funded by the business, which is owned by about 65 members of the founding family and chaired by the eighth-generation John Smedley descendant Ian Maclean.

The first in a line of John Smedleys was brought in to manage the original factory, owned by the family of Florence Nightingale. The Smedleys took control of the business, then making spun cotton and muslin, in 1818, eventually adapting it to spin wool and cotton yarns and then knit them into clothing.

By the mid-1800s the company had made a name crafting underwear, with some claiming that the term long johns takes its name from John Smedley. The John Smedley brand itself was first registered in 1876 and by the end of the century it had diversified into men’s clothing.

In 1932, Smedley’s knitting machines began making the three-button polo shirt, still one of its bestsellers. By the 50s and 60s the brand’s fame was at its height, with celebrities such as Marilyn Monroe, the Beatles and Audrey Hepburn photographed wearing John Smedley roll necks.
Today, John Smedley sells around the world via its website and a string of stores in Japan, as well as in two London boutiques and luxury outlets including Selfridges, Harrods and Brown Thomas.

The urbane British actor Bill Nighy recently collaborated with the label on two collections, having worn its three-button polo shirt since he was 17. The brand also created a cheaper diffusion line, JS, which was sold in John Lewis in 2024 and is now sold via the Smedley website and in Japan.

paragraphs.zh: 1932 年，Smedley 的针织机开始生产三粒扣 polo 衫，这款至今仍是其最畅销的产品之一。到五六十年代，品牌声名达到顶峰，玛丽莲·梦露、披头士乐队和奥黛丽·赫本等名人都曾被拍到穿着 John Smedley 的高领针织衫。

paragraphs.en: Today, John Smedley sells around the world via its website and a string of stores in Japan, as well as in two London boutiques and luxury outlets including Selfridges, Harrods and Brown Thomas.
paragraphs.zh: 如今，John Smedley 通过自有网站和在日本的一系列门店销往全球，此外还在伦敦的两家精品店，以及 Selfridges、Harrods、Brown Thomas 等高端百货渠道销售。

paragraphs.en: The urbane British actor Bill Nighy recently collaborated with the label on two collections, having worn its three-button polo shirt since he was 17. The brand also created a cheaper diffusion line, JS, which was sold in John Lewis in 2024 and is now sold via the Smedley website and in Japan.
paragraphs.zh: 温文尔雅的英国演员比尔·奈伊（Bill Nighy）最近与该品牌合作推出两个系列——他从 17 岁起就穿其三粒扣 polo 衫。品牌还推出了一条价格更亲民的副线 JS，2024 年曾在 John Lewis 百货销售，目前通过 Smedley 官网及在日本销售。

sentences.en: The brand’s site in the Peak District, Derbyshire, is the oldest continuously operating factory in the world, with a maze of buildings, one of which dates to 1784.
sentences.structure: 主干：The site is the factory（主系表）。修饰：in the Peak District, Derbyshire 为后置地点定语；oldest continuously operating 为形容词最高级叠加分词定语，修饰 factory；with a maze of buildings 为 with 复合结构补充说明厂区形态；one of which dates to 1784 为非限制性关系从句，先行词是 buildings。
sentences.analysis_zh: 主句把“厂区即工厂”直接等同，是为了强调品牌与厂址一体、生产未曾中断这一核心卖点。“continuously operating”是关键限定语，缺了它“最古老”就站不住。后面的 with 结构和关系从句都是补充信息，翻译时可拆成短句，避免中文一句话过长。

sentences.en: There are 3,515 manufacturers of clothing in the UK, according to figures from the Office for National Statistics collated by UKFT, 315 fewer than a decade before.
sentences.structure: 主干：There are 3,515 manufacturers（there be 存在句）。修饰：of clothing in the UK 限定 manufacturers；according to figures... 为介词短语作状语，说明数据来源；collated by UKFT 为过去分词短语后置修饰 figures；315 fewer than a decade before 为比较结构，作补充说明，逻辑上指代前面的人数。
sentences.analysis_zh: 新闻英语典型的数据句：先给数字，再用 according to 交代来源（并顺带点出数据经过行业协会二次整理，暗示可信度），最后用省略式的“315 fewer than...”给出对比。中文宜把来源前置或另起一句，否则数字和对比会挤在一起。

sentences.en: The company is not struggling to attract new workers as, McGuire-Dudley says, young people are interested in craft skills and the sustainability aspect of making goods closer to home.
sentences.structure: 主干：The company is not struggling to attract new workers（主系表，表语为动名词短语）。修饰：as 引导原因状语从句，说明“不缺人”的原因；McGuire-Dudley says 为插入语，插在 as 之后是出于英语的句法习惯（避免与从句主语连读歧义）；从句内 interested in 后接两个并列宾语 craft skills 与 the sustainability aspect...，其中 of making goods closer to home 修饰 aspect。
sentences.analysis_zh: 注意 as 在此表“因为”，不是“当……时”。插入语位置别扭但符合英语新闻写作规范：把说话人放在连词后面，既标明了信息来源，又不打断主句节奏。翻译时把插入语提到句首（“她说”）最自然。

background.title: 皇家认证（Royal Warrant）
background.text_zh: 皇家认证是英国王室授予长期向王室供应商品或服务的商家的正式标志，由君主或王室高级成员签发，通常需有多年供货记录才可申请，并定期复核。获得认证的品牌可在包装和宣传中使用王室徽记，这在英国被视为品质与传统的老牌背书，对出口（尤其日本、美国市场）尤其有加分作用。文中提到查尔斯国王与卡米拉王后分别颁授，说明该企业同时持有不止一份认证。

background.title: 英国服装制造的离岸外包与行业统计
background.text_zh: 20 世纪后半叶起，英国服装业大规模把生产转移到劳动力成本更低的亚洲国家，本土留下的是设计、营销、零售与少量高端制造。文中的两个数据来源值得留意：英国国家统计局（ONS）是官方统计机构，而 UKFT（英国时尚与纺织协会）是行业协会——行业数据常由协会“整理”官方数字后发布，因此报道才会写“collated by UKFT”。理解这一点，有助于判断文中 3515 家制造商、1.5 万从业者这类数字的口径。

title_en: Rare beetle that oozes substance from its knees when attacked rediscovered in Wales
excerpt_en: Natural Resources Wales says short-necked oil beetle has been found in country for first time in nearly 60 years
body_en: A rare beetle has been rediscovered in Wales after nearly 60 years, conservationists have said.

The short-necked oil beetle, driven to the brink of extinction in Britain due to habitat loss over the course of the 20th century, has been found at the Castlemartin range in Pembrokeshire, according to Natural Resources Wales (NRW).
The species’ name comes from the adult beetles’ stubby shape and ability to secrete an oily yellow-orange substance from their knee joints when alarmed.

The unusual creature relies on solitary bees and thick vegetation and flower coverage to survive. Its larvae have hook-like feet to snag on to bees, and once in their nest, they feed on pollen until ready to emerge as adults, with a lifespan of about a year.
Only a handful of sites in the UK are suitable for the beetle, according to NRW, and only about one in 10,000 larvae make it to adulthood. It is classed as nationally rare.
The bug was rediscovered in Devon in 2006, and populations have since been found in the Hebrides and on Salisbury Plain.
Related: Warning over ‘fab four’ oil beetles

The nature conservation charity Buglife reported the beetle was found at the Pembrokeshire site in 2020, but surveys carried out in 2022 and 2025 only found dead adults, raising concerns about the species’ viability in the area.
However, the 2026 survey discovered larvae distributed in such a way to suggest hatchlings from a larger batch of immature beetles had thrived.
Anna Hobbs, the project delivery officer for the Bumblebee Conservation Trust, said finding evidence the species was breeding again was very exciting.

“The short-necked oil beetle is an amazing creature and not only depends on a very specific habitat to survive, but the presence of solitary bees as well. So, the work we do needs to consider the needs of several species to be effective,” she said.

“We are very grateful to our partners and volunteers for persevering with us after two years without larval sightings and look forward to the continued management of the site so that this amazing species can survive now and into the future.”

The beetle project, part of Wales’s flagship species recovery programme, Natur am Byth, is working to conserve several endangered animals and plants that share similar habitats to the short-necked oil beetle, including the shrill carder bee, goldilocks aster and pale dog violet.

enrich.title_zh: 在威尔士消失近60年的稀有甲虫重现
enrich.summary_zh: 一种因栖息地丧失而在英国濒临灭绝的稀有甲虫——短颈油甲虫，在威尔士彭布罗克郡的卡斯尔马丁靶场被重新发现，距上次记录已近60年。这种甲虫依赖独居蜂和特定植被生存，幼虫存活率仅约万分之一。虽然2020年曾在当地发现个体，但随后几年只找到死亡成虫；直到2026年的调查发现幼虫分布迹象，才表明该物种正在重新繁殖。

paragraphs.en: A rare beetle has been rediscovered in Wales after nearly 60 years, conservationists have said.
paragraphs.zh: 环保人士表示，一种稀有甲虫在阔别近60年后，于威尔士被重新发现。

paragraphs.en: The short-necked oil beetle, driven to the brink of extinction in Britain due to habitat loss over the course of the 20th century, has been found at the Castlemartin range in Pembrokeshire, according to Natural Resources Wales (NRW).
paragraphs.zh: 据威尔士自然资源部（NRW）称，这种短颈油甲虫是在彭布罗克郡的卡斯尔马丁靶场被发现的。由于20世纪期间栖息地不断丧失，它在英国已被逼到灭绝的边缘。

paragraphs.en: The species’ name comes from the adult beetles’ stubby shape and ability to secrete an oily yellow-orange substance from their knee joints when alarmed.
paragraphs.zh: 这一物种的名字来自成年甲虫粗短的身形，以及它们在受惊时能从膝关节分泌出一种油状黄橙色物质的能力。

paragraphs.en: The unusual creature relies on solitary bees and thick vegetation and flower coverage to survive. Its larvae have hook-like feet to snag on to bees, and once in their nest, they feed on pollen until ready to emerge as adults, with a lifespan of about a year.
paragraphs.zh: 这种奇特的生物依靠独居蜂以及茂密的植被和花丛生存。它的幼虫长有钩状足，可以钩住蜜蜂；一旦进入蜂巢，它们便以花粉为食，直到羽化为成虫，寿命约为一年。

paragraphs.en: Only a handful of sites in the UK are suitable for the beetle, according to NRW, and only about one in 10,000 larvae make it to adulthood. It is classed as nationally rare.
paragraphs.zh: 据威尔士自然资源部介绍，英国只有少数几个地点适合这种甲虫生存，而且大约每1万只幼虫中只有一只能够活到成年。它被列为国家稀有物种。

paragraphs.en: The bug was rediscovered in Devon in 2006, and populations have since been found in the Hebrides and on Salisbury Plain.
paragraphs.zh: 这种甲虫曾于2006年在德文郡被重新发现，此后又在赫布里底群岛和索尔兹伯里平原发现了种群。

paragraphs.en: Related: Warning over ‘fab four’ oil beetles
paragraphs.zh: 相关报道：关于“四甲虫”油甲虫的警告

paragraphs.en: The nature conservation charity Buglife reported the beetle was found at the Pembrokeshire site in 2020, but surveys carried out in 2022 and 2025 only found dead adults, raising concerns about the species’ viability in the area.
paragraphs.zh: 自然保护慈善机构“虫子生活”（Buglife）报告称，该甲虫于2020年在彭布罗克郡的这一地点被发现，但2022年和2025年开展的调查只发现了死亡的成虫，这让人们担忧该物种在这一地区是否还能存续。

paragraphs.en: However, the 2026 survey discovered larvae distributed in such a way to suggest hatchlings from a larger batch of immature beetles had thrived.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，2026年的调查发现了幼虫，其分布方式表明，来自更大一批未成熟甲虫的幼体已经存活并成长起来。

paragraphs.en: Anna Hobbs, the project delivery officer for the Bumblebee Conservation Trust, said finding evidence the species was breeding again was very exciting.
paragraphs.zh: 大黄蜂保护信托基金的项目执行官员安娜·霍布斯表示，找到该物种再次繁殖的证据令人非常振奋。

paragraphs.en: “The short-necked oil beetle is an amazing creature and not only depends on a very specific habitat to survive, but the presence of solitary bees as well. So, the work we do needs to consider the needs of several species to be effective,” she said.
paragraphs.zh: 她说：“短颈油甲虫是一种奇妙的生物，它不仅依赖非常特定的栖息地才能生存，还需要独居蜂的存在。因此，我们所做的工作必须兼顾多个物种的需求，才能取得成效。”

paragraphs.en: “We are very grateful to our partners and volunteers for persevering with us after two years without larval sightings and look forward to the continued management of the site so that this amazing species can survive now and into the future.”
paragraphs.zh: “我们非常感谢合作伙伴和志愿者，在连续两年没有发现幼虫踪迹之后仍与我们一道坚持不懈；我们也期待继续对该地点进行管理，让这一奇妙物种如今乃至未来都能生存下去。”

paragraphs.en: The beetle project, part of Wales’s flagship species recovery programme, Natur am Byth, is working to conserve several endangered animals and plants that share similar habitats to the short-necked oil beetle, including the shrill carder bee, goldilocks aster and pale dog violet.
paragraphs.zh: 这项甲虫项目是威尔士旗舰物种恢复计划“Natur am Byth”的一部分，致力于保护多种与短颈油甲虫共享相似栖息地的濒危动植物，包括高音熊蜂、金发紫菀和淡色堇菜。

sentences.en: The short-necked oil beetle, driven to the brink of extinction in Britain due to habitat loss over the course of the 20th century, has been found at the Castlemartin range in Pembrokeshire, according to Natural Resources Wales (NRW).
sentences.structure: 主干：The short-necked oil beetle ... has been found at the Castlemartin range in Pembrokeshire；修饰：过去分词短语 driven to the brink of extinction ... 作后置定语插入主谓之间；according to Natural Resources Wales 为信息来源状语。
sentences.analysis_zh: 主语和谓语被一个较长的过去分词短语隔开，这种插入式定语在新闻英语中很常见：先把物种的处境作为背景交代清楚，再落到“被发现”这个新闻点。driven to the brink of extinction 是“被逼到灭绝边缘”，due to habitat loss 说明原因，over the course of the 20th century 限定时间跨度。句末 according to 引出消息来源，体现报道的严谨性。翻译时把长定语拆成独立一句更符合中文习惯。

sentences.en: Its larvae have hook-like feet to snag on to bees, and once in their nest, they feed on pollen until ready to emerge as adults, with a lifespan of about a year.
sentences.structure: 并列句：① Its larvae have hook-like feet to snag on to bees（目的不定式作状语）；② once in their nest, they feed on pollen until ready to emerge as adults（once in their nest 为省略式状语从句 = once they are in their nest；until ready 亦为省略结构 = until they are ready）；with a lifespan of about a year 为补充说明的 with 复合结构。
sentences.analysis_zh: 两个分句按时间顺序叙述幼虫的生命周期：先靠钩状足钩住蜜蜂（snag on to），进入蜂巢后吃花粉，直到羽化。once in their nest 和 until ready to emerge 都是省略了主语和 be 动词的状语从句，这是英语里常见的“连词+形容词或介词短语”精简写法。句末 with a lifespan... 起补充信息作用，中文可译为单独一句。“be ready to do”在这里不是“准备好”，而是“发育成熟、可以……”。

sentences.en: The beetle project, part of Wales’s flagship species recovery programme, Natur am Byth, is working to conserve several endangered animals and plants that share similar habitats to the short-necked oil beetle, including the shrill carder bee, goldilocks aster and pale dog violet.
sentences.structure: 主干：The beetle project ... is working to conserve several endangered animals and plants；修饰：part of Wales’s flagship species recovery programme, Natur am Byth 为同位语；that share similar habitats to the short-necked oil beetle 为定语从句修饰 animals and plants；including ... 举例补充。
sentences.analysis_zh: 主语后连续两个同位成分交代项目背景，信息密度很高，中文宜拆句处理。定语从句 that share similar habitats to... 用 share ... with 的变体 share similar habitats to，说明保护逻辑：一个地点的栖息地可以同时供养多个濒危物种，因此保护工作是“打包”进行的。including 后面并列三个物种名，都是英国特有的珍稀动植物。

background.title: 威尔士自然资源部与“具有国家意义的稀有物种”
background.text_zh: Natural Resources Wales（NRW）是威尔士政府的法定环境机构，负责管理自然保护、林业、水资源和部分军事用地上的生态监测。文章中提到的“nationally rare”（国家稀有）是英国一种正式的物种分级标准，通常指在英国境内的分布点少于15个的物种，比“濒危”在保护优先级上略低一级，但仍受重点关注。

background.title: 卡斯尔马丁靶场与“Natur am Byth”计划
background.text_zh: Castlemartin range 位于威尔士西南端的彭布罗克郡海岸，是英国国防部使用的装甲射击训练场。由于长期不进行农业开垦，靶场内部保留了大量的原生草地和野花群落，反而成为许多稀有昆虫（包括多种油甲虫和熊蜂）的避难所，通常是“军事用地+生态保护”合作管理的典型例子。Natur am Byth（威尔士语，意为“永恒的自然”）是威尔士近年启动的旗舰性物种恢复计划，由多个保护组织和政府机构联合执行，目标是在特定地点同时恢复多个共享栖息地的濒危物种。

title_en: Sadiq Khan calls for cap on numbers of robotaxis on London streets
excerpt_en: Mayor questions impact on air quality, congestion and jobs as government poised to allow driverless vehicles in capital
body_en: London’s mayor has called for a cap on the numbers of robotaxis on its streets, with the UK government poised to allow fully driverless vehicles to operate in the capital.

Sadiq Khan said politicians had failed to “grasp the pace of change” from the technology, which could threaten jobs and increase congestion in the city, and questioned whether the rules for autonomous cars were fit for purpose.
His comments came after Chinese robotaxis, now being tested in London, were unveiled by Freenow by Lyft, a rival to Uber.
In September Uber started offering limited passenger services in Wayve’s self-driving cars, albeit with a safety driver in the front seat, under licence from Transport for London (TfL).
Freenow by Lyft is hoping to launch fully driverless Baidu robotaxis as early as next year, under a national licensing scheme.

However, the companies, as well as Waymo – which operates robotaxis in San Francisco and other US cities – are primarily focusing on London and Khan said the city needed to be able to limit the rollout.

“What we don’t want is a situation where there’s a big bang without proper regulation in place. We’ve got to make sure the regulation is fit for purpose before we have a mass rollout of things like automated vehicles,” said Khan.

He added: “I think the pace of change when it comes to tech and innovation has not been fully grasped by politicians. There’s got to be incremental movement when it comes to things like robotaxis or automated vehicles.
“We’re lobbying the government for TfL, for London, to have more powers than it currently has on things like automated vehicles.

“There are big questions that haven’t been answered yet: what impact will this have on air quality, on congestion, on those people whose livelihood is being a private hire vehicle driver or a black-taxi driver.”
Related: Uber begins self-driving robotaxi trial in Manchester
Drivers’ unions have held protests at the London HQs of Wayve and Waymo in recent weeks, with many Uber drivers fearing for their future.
Khan added: “Is there going to be a cap? At the moment there’s no cap on the number of private hire vehicles or taxis. We’ve lobbied for those powers as well.
“London isn’t San Francisco. We’re a city of almost 10 million, 400 villages, narrow roads, and it’s really important to get this right.”

Under current regulations for fully autonomous vehicles, TfL can only give or refuse consent for their use within London and not manage or license robotaxi services, making the capital’s authorities somewhat less enthusiastic than ministers to accelerate towards the new technology.
However, Freenow by Lyft said the UK’s national framework for driverless cars was an important factor.

Danny O’Gorman, UK and Ireland general manager, said it was “great news for us to really invest in the market. But in terms of how it’s going to be regulated, once the service is up and running, that’s something that still needs to be ironed out.”
O’Gorman said the company was working closely with TfL and “wanted to do things the right way”. About 24 autonomous Baidu Apollo Go vehicles are being tested in the London borough of Brent.

The spacious Chinese cars, which incorporate a massage seat and a built-in touchscreen in the back for passengers, are in fully autonomous service in cities in China and the UAE, and appeared to be handling the streets safely in a test drive in October for the Guardian.

But many test trips still require human intervention, with roadworks proving difficult. For autonomous vehicles (AVs), “an interesting challenge in London is following the rules of the road”, when many drivers ignore them, O’Gorman said: “You get beeped at a lot for following the speed limit.”
Freenow by Lyft is promising a purpose-built AV depot in the UK. O’Gorman said a large proportion of displaced taxi drivers could be employed there in remote operating and servicing jobs.

The company has traditionally worked with black cabs and, he said: “The larger risks to that industry are the driver age profile: two-thirds are over 50 and they’re retiring, and the vehicle’s too expensive.

enrich.title_zh: 萨迪克·汗呼吁为伦敦街头的 Robotaxi 数量设定上限
enrich.summary_zh: 伦敦市长萨迪克·汗呼吁对市内自动驾驶出租车的数量设上限，批评政界未充分认识技术变革的速度，并质疑现行规则是否管用。目前百度 Apollo Go 正在伦敦布伦特区测试，Uber 与 Wayve 也已提供有限载客服务，但伦敦交通局无权管理或发放 Robotaxi 牌照。汗要求下放相关权力，并关注就业、拥堵与空气质量；司机工会已发起抗议。

paragraphs.en: London’s mayor has called for a cap on the numbers of robotaxis on its streets, with the UK government poised to allow fully driverless vehicles to operate in the capital.
paragraphs.zh: 伦敦市长呼吁对市内街道上的 Robotaxi（自动驾驶出租车）数量设定上限，而英国政府正准备允许完全无人驾驶车辆在首都上路运营。

paragraphs.en: Sadiq Khan said politicians had failed to “grasp the pace of change” from the technology, which could threaten jobs and increase congestion in the city, and questioned whether the rules for autonomous cars were fit for purpose.
paragraphs.zh: 萨迪克·汗表示，政界人士未能“把握这项技术带来的变化速度”，而该技术可能威胁就业、加剧城市拥堵；他还质疑针对自动驾驶汽车的规则是否真正适用。

paragraphs.en: His comments came after Chinese robotaxis, now being tested in London, were unveiled by Freenow by Lyft, a rival to Uber.
paragraphs.zh: 他发表上述言论之前，Lyft 旗下的 Freenow 刚刚展示了正在伦敦测试的中国 Robotaxi，该公司是 Uber 的竞争对手。

paragraphs.en: In September Uber started offering limited passenger services in Wayve’s self-driving cars, albeit with a safety driver in the front seat, under licence from Transport for London (TfL).
paragraphs.zh: 今年 9 月，Uber 在获得伦敦交通局（TfL）许可的情况下，开始用 Wayve 的自动驾驶汽车提供有限的载客服务，不过前排仍配有一名安全员。

paragraphs.en: Freenow by Lyft is hoping to launch fully driverless Baidu robotaxis as early as next year, under a national licensing scheme.
paragraphs.zh: Freenow 希望最早于明年依据全国性许可制度，推出完全无人驾驶的百度 Robotaxi。

paragraphs.en: However, the companies, as well as Waymo – which operates robotaxis in San Francisco and other US cities – are primarily focusing on London and Khan said the city needed to be able to limit the rollout.
paragraphs.zh: 不过，这些公司以及 Waymo（在旧金山等美国城市运营 Robotaxi）主要都把重点放在伦敦，而汗表示，伦敦需要有能力限制其推广规模。

paragraphs.en: “What we don’t want is a situation where there’s a big bang without proper regulation in place. We’ve got to make sure the regulation is fit for purpose before we have a mass rollout of things like automated vehicles,” said Khan.
paragraphs.zh: “我们不希望出现的情况是，在缺乏适当监管的情况下一下子全面铺开。在自动驾驶车辆这类东西大规模上路之前，我们必须确保监管切实有效。”汗说。

paragraphs.en: He added: “I think the pace of change when it comes to tech and innovation has not been fully grasped by politicians. There’s got to be incremental movement when it comes to things like robotaxis or automated vehicles.
paragraphs.zh: 他补充道：“我认为，政界人士尚未充分把握科技与创新领域的变化速度。在 Robotaxi 或自动驾驶车辆这类事情上，必须循序渐进。”

paragraphs.en: “We’re lobbying the government for TfL, for London, to have more powers than it currently has on things like automated vehicles.
paragraphs.zh: “我们正在游说政府，让伦敦交通局、让伦敦在自动驾驶车辆等问题上拥有比现在更大的权力。”

paragraphs.en: “There are big questions that haven’t been answered yet: what impact will this have on air quality, on congestion, on those people whose livelihood is being a private hire vehicle driver or a black-taxi driver.”
paragraphs.zh: “还有一些重大问题尚未得到解答：这将对空气质量、对交通拥堵、对那些靠开网约车或黑色出租车谋生的人产生什么影响。”

paragraphs.en: Related: Uber begins self-driving robotaxi trial in Manchester
paragraphs.zh: 相关报道：Uber 在曼彻斯特启动自动驾驶 Robotaxi 试运营

paragraphs.en: Drivers’ unions have held protests at the London HQs of Wayve and Waymo in recent weeks, with many Uber drivers fearing for their future.
paragraphs.zh: 近几周，司机工会已在 Wayve 和 Waymo 的伦敦总部外举行抗议，许多 Uber 司机对自己的前途感到担忧。

paragraphs.en: Khan added: “Is there going to be a cap? At the moment there’s no cap on the number of private hire vehicles or taxis. We’ve lobbied for those powers as well.
paragraphs.zh: 汗补充说：“会不会设上限？目前对网约车和出租车的数量并没有上限。我们也一直在为获得这方面的权力而游说。”

paragraphs.en: “London isn’t San Francisco. We’re a city of almost 10 million, 400 villages, narrow roads, and it’s really important to get this right.”
paragraphs.zh: “伦敦不是旧金山。我们是一座拥有近 1000 万人口、400 个‘村庄’、道路狭窄的城市，把这件事做对非常重要。”

paragraphs.en: Under current regulations for fully autonomous vehicles, TfL can only give or refuse consent for their use within London and not manage or license robotaxi services, making the capital’s authorities somewhat less enthusiastic than ministers to accelerate towards the new technology.
paragraphs.zh: 按照现行针对完全自动驾驶车辆的规定，伦敦交通局只能就是否同意其在伦敦使用表示同意或拒绝，而无权管理 Robotaxi 服务或为其发放牌照；这使得伦敦当局在加速拥抱这项新技术上，不如中央政府部长们那么积极。

paragraphs.en: However, Freenow by Lyft said the UK’s national framework for driverless cars was an important factor.
paragraphs.zh: 不过，Freenow 表示，英国全国性的无人驾驶汽车框架是一个重要因素。

paragraphs.en: Danny O’Gorman, UK and Ireland general manager, said it was “great news for us to really invest in the market. But in terms of how it’s going to be regulated, once the service is up and running, that’s something that still needs to be ironed out.”
paragraphs.zh: 该公司英国与爱尔兰区总经理丹尼·奥戈尔曼表示，“对我们来说，能够真正投入这个市场是个好消息。但至于服务上线运营后如何监管，这一点仍有待厘清。”

paragraphs.en: O’Gorman said the company was working closely with TfL and “wanted to do things the right way”. About 24 autonomous Baidu Apollo Go vehicles are being tested in the London borough of Brent.
paragraphs.zh: 奥戈尔曼说，公司正与伦敦交通局密切合作，“希望把事情做对”。目前约有 24 辆百度 Apollo Go 自动驾驶车辆在伦敦布伦特区测试。

paragraphs.en: The spacious Chinese cars, which incorporate a massage seat and a built-in touchscreen in the back for passengers, are in fully autonomous service in cities in China and the UAE, and appeared to be handling the streets safely in a test drive in October for the Guardian.
paragraphs.zh: 这些宽敞的中国车配有按摩座椅，后排还为乘客内置了触屏。它们已在中国和阿联酋的多个城市投入完全自动驾驶服务；在《卫报》10 月的一次试乘中，它们似乎能安全地应对街道行驶。

paragraphs.en: But many test trips still require human intervention, with roadworks proving difficult. For autonomous vehicles (AVs), “an interesting challenge in London is following the rules of the road”, when many drivers ignore them, O’Gorman said: “You get beeped at a lot for following the speed limit.”
paragraphs.zh: 但许多测试行程仍需要人工介入，道路施工就是一大难点。奥戈尔曼说，对自动驾驶汽车（AV）来说，“在伦敦一个有趣的挑战是遵守交通规则”，因为很多司机并不遵守：“你按规定限速行驶，就会被按喇叭按个不停。”

paragraphs.en: Freenow by Lyft is promising a purpose-built AV depot in the UK. O’Gorman said a large proportion of displaced taxi drivers could be employed there in remote operating and servicing jobs.
paragraphs.zh: Freenow 承诺在英国建设专门的自动驾驶车辆场站。奥戈尔曼表示，很大一部分被取代的出租车司机可以在那里从事远程操作和车辆维护工作。

paragraphs.en: The company has traditionally worked with black cabs and, he said: “The larger risks to that industry are the driver age profile: two-thirds are over 50 and they’re retiring, and the vehicle’s too expensive.
paragraphs.zh: 该公司一向与黑色出租车（black cab）合作。他说：“这个行业更大的风险在于司机的年龄结构：三分之二的人超过 50 岁，正在陆续退休，而且车辆也太贵了。”

vocab.meaning_zh: 上限；封顶额度（常与 on 连用：a cap on sth）
vocab.example_en: The mayor wants a cap on the number of robotaxis allowed in the city.
vocab.example_zh: 市长希望为市内允许运营的 Robotaxi 数量设定上限。

vocab.meaning_zh: 准备就绪的，即将（做某事）的（poised to do sth）
vocab.example_en: The government is poised to approve fully driverless cars.
vocab.example_zh: 政府正准备批准完全无人驾驶汽车。

vocab.meaning_zh: （规则、制度等）适合其用途的，切实管用的；英式政治与媒体高频表达
vocab.example_en: Critics say the current rules are not fit for purpose.
vocab.example_zh: 批评者称现行规则并不适用。

vocab.meaning_zh: 领会，充分理解（抽象事物，如变化速度、复杂性）
vocab.example_en: Politicians have not grasped how fast the technology is moving.
vocab.example_zh: 政界人士没有充分意识到这项技术发展得有多快。

vocab.meaning_zh: （新产品、新服务的）推广，铺开，投放
vocab.example_en: The rollout of robotaxis will start in a few boroughs.
vocab.example_zh: Robotaxi 的推广将先从几个区开始。

vocab.meaning_zh: （政策、改革）一次性全面铺开、骤然启动（与渐进式 incremental 相对）
vocab.example_en: He opposes a big bang approach to opening the market.
vocab.example_zh: 他反对以“一步到位”的方式开放市场。

vocab.meaning_zh: 逐步的，渐进式的，小幅递增的
vocab.example_en: Change in this industry tends to be incremental rather than sudden.
vocab.example_zh: 这个行业的变化往往是渐进的，而非突变的。

vocab.meaning_zh: 游说（lobby sb for sth：为争取某事而游说某人）
vocab.example_en: The city is lobbying ministers for extra regulatory powers.
vocab.example_zh: 该市正在游说部长们给予更多监管权力。

vocab.meaning_zh: （英国）预约式载客车辆，即网约车/租赁用车，须持 TfL 牌照，区别于可路边扬招的黑色出租车
vocab.example_en: Private hire vehicle drivers must be licensed by Transport for London.
vocab.example_zh: 网约车司机必须获得伦敦交通局的执照。

vocab.meaning_zh: （通过讨论）解决、消除（问题、分歧、细节）
vocab.example_en: There are still details to be ironed out before the launch.
vocab.example_zh: 上线之前仍有一些细节需要敲定。

vocab.meaning_zh: 被迫离开原有岗位的，被取代的（displaced workers）
vocab.example_en: The firm says it can retrain displaced drivers.
vocab.example_zh: 该公司称可以为被取代的司机提供再培训。

sentences.en: Sadiq Khan said politicians had failed to “grasp the pace of change” from the technology, which could threaten jobs and increase congestion in the city, and questioned whether the rules for autonomous cars were fit for purpose.
sentences.structure: 主干：Sadiq Khan said (that) ... and questioned whether ...（两个并列谓语 said / questioned 共用一个主语）。said 后接宾语从句 politicians had failed to grasp...，用过去完成时表示“先于说话时已未能做到”；which could threaten jobs and increase congestion 是非限制性定语从句，先行词是 the technology，说明其潜在后果；questioned 后接 whether 引导的宾语从句作宾语。
sentences.analysis_zh: 这句话把“陈述”和“质疑”两个动作并列，是新闻报道中压缩引语信息的常用写法：先给事实（说了什么），再给态度（质疑什么）。注意 the technology 后面跟了两个 which 从句式的后果（威胁就业、加剧拥堵），但它们属于说话人的判断，而非本报记者的断言，因此用 could 而非 will，翻译时也应保留“可能”这层语气。

sentences.en: Under current regulations for fully autonomous vehicles, TfL can only give or refuse consent for their use within London and not manage or license robotaxi services, making the capital’s authorities somewhat less enthusiastic than ministers to accelerate towards the new technology.
sentences.structure: 主干：TfL can only give or refuse consent ... and not manage or license robotaxi services。句首 Under current regulations ... 是状语前置，交代法律前提；making ... 是现在分词短语作结果状语，逻辑主语是整个前面那件事（TfL 权限有限），而不是 TfL 本身；less enthusiastic than ministers 是形容词比较级结构，后面 to accelerate 说明在什么事情上不那么积极。
sentences.analysis_zh: 英文常用“分词短语作结果状语”来把因果关系压进一个长句，中文则更习惯拆成两个短句或用“这使得……”。翻译时把这个 making 译成“这使得”最自然。另外 authority（常用复数 the authorities）在政治新闻里指“当局、主管部门”，不是“权威”；minister 指中央政府部长，这里与 London 的市一级机构形成中央对地方的对照。

sentences.en: The spacious Chinese cars, which incorporate a massage seat and a built-in touchscreen in the back for passengers, are in fully autonomous service in cities in China and the UAE, and appeared to be handling the streets safely in a test drive in October for the Guardian.
sentences.structure: 主干：The spacious Chinese cars are in fully autonomous service ... and appeared to be handling the streets safely ...（两个并列谓语）。which incorporate ... 是非限制性定语从句，补充配置信息，可视为插入语，去掉不影响主干；in cities in China and the UAE 是地点状语；appeared to be handling 中的 appear to 表示记者基于观察所做的谨慎判断。
sentences.analysis_zh: 这句是典型的“名词+长定语从句+双谓语”结构，主语被从句隔开，读者容易在 are 之前迷路——抓住 The spacious Chinese cars ... are ... 就通了。appear to be doing 是外刊常用的“留有余地”表达：记者亲历试乘，但不下断言，只说“看起来处理得安全”，比 handled safely safely 更符合新闻规范，译成“似乎能安全应对”最贴切。

background.title: 英国自动驾驶的立法与监管分工
background.text_zh: 英国在 2024 年通过《自动驾驶汽车法》（Automated Vehicles Act 2024），为无人驾驶车辆在英格兰、威尔士和苏格兰上路建立全国性许可与责任框架，相关细则仍在分阶段落地，这也是文中“national licensing scheme”“national framework”所指。制度上的关键点在于：全国性框架由中央政府（交通部及其车辆认证机构）主导，而伦敦交通局（TfL）作为地方交通主管机构，对伦敦出租车与网约车（private hire）历来拥有牌照与数量管理权，却对新型 Robotaxi 服务缺少对应的许可与管理权限——这正是汗要求“下放权力”的制度背景。

background.title: 伦敦的出租车生态与“400 个村庄”
background.text_zh: 伦敦载客车辆大体分为两类：可路边扬招的黑色出租车（black cab，司机须通过严格的“知识考试”The Knowledge），以及必须提前预约的 private hire vehicle（网约车、专车，含 Uber、Freenow 等平台车辆）。二者由 TfL 分别发牌管理，历史上对数量、准入有过多次收紧与争议，因此“要不要设上限”在伦敦是长期政治议题。至于“400 villages”，是伦敦人自嘲式的说法：这座城市由众多原本独立的村镇街区拼接而成，彼此界限分明，与曼哈顿式的网格或旧金山的规整路网差别很大——这正是汗强调“伦敦不是旧金山”、也是自动驾驶公司承认本地路况难的原因。

title_en: Dafne Keen and Harriet Walter on working with Patrick Stewart: ‘I’ve never seen anyone so ecstatic’
excerpt_en: The late actor’s co-stars in Logan and Anthony and Cleopatra remember dog impressions, marching band-conducting and a fervent belief in fun
body_en: Dafne Keen: ‘He asked me: have you noticed no-one ever sneezes in films?’ I had the unbelievable privilege of working with Patrick when I was 11 [in Logan]. He was a man of extraordinary warmth, wit and generosity. He possessed that increasingly rare ability to make everyone around him feel as though they were being let in on something wonderful. To work alongside him was to be reminded, every day, of what it means to love what you do, and to share that love with others. He imparted lessons in a way that was so wise, you didn’t even realise you were being taught.

To describe Patrick simply as a remarkable man would feel an injustice to the sheer breadth of what made him so. He was a master of his craft, certainly, but also a teacher, a raconteur, a mischief-maker and, above all, a profoundly generous human being. He carried his knowledge lightly, his humour generously, and his affection for the people around him with a warmth that was impossible to miss.

He had a seemingly inexhaustible supply of jokes that could make the longest, most arduous days on set pass in minutes. I remember walking around one of the house sets with him and remarking that the only thing missing from the home was a dog. Without missing a beat, Patrick began barking and behaving like one, until I was absolutely roaring with laughter. It was that sort of instinctive silliness, a complete willingness to abandon any notion of grandeur or self-importance, that made being around him such a joy.

He was equally gifted at talking to children and professors alike, shifting his linguistic code to meet whoever happened to be in front of him. I remember the little snippets of Shakespeare, Ibsen, Chekhov and Pinter he would spontaneously grace us with, sharing passages from the works he loved as though letting us in on a private little world. He could move from the most sophisticated literary conversation to the most ridiculous schoolyard mischief without ever seeming to change gear.

Patrick was an incredibly protective scene partner and colleague. He had a way of making you feel included, listened to and respected, even when you were just a clueless 11-year-old finding your feet in the pressure-filled adult world of a film set. I remember him noticing me looking longingly at his Professor X wheelchair, and secretly approaching me to explain that if you pushed the stick hard enough, it went very, very fast. He then proceeded to invite me on it, encouraging me to go faster. I remember him hatching little plans with me, things we could sneak into scenes to make the set feel more like a playground and less like the intimidating grown-up world it could sometimes be.

On one of our first days together, after an incredibly intense take, he turned to me and asked, entirely seriously, “Have you ever noticed, no one ever sneezes in films?” I stared at him for a moment before agreeing that he was quite right. “We should try to sneeze in this one,” he said. And so we made a pact to try to sneak a sneeze into a take. It was such a Patrick observation: at once completely absurd and rather brilliant. He was an artist with an extraordinary attentiveness to the world around him, someone who noticed the smallest details and understood that there was always something worth questioning, even in the most familiar conventions of his craft.

That was perhaps one of the loveliest things about him. He never seemed to outgrow the joy of playing, or to lose sight of the fact that, at its heart, acting should be fun. He had this extraordinary ability to make you feel that you weren’t simply there to do a job, but to be part of something, to contribute, to experiment and, above all, to enjoy yourself.

There is something incredibly moving about the idea that an actor of his stature never made a child feel small, inexperienced or peripheral. He let you in on the secret. He made you feel like a fellow conspirator, a teammate.

I learnt so much from him. He was, however briefly, my colleague and my acting professor, and he will forever be my Professor X. Someone who built a little safe haven for me on the often alien world of a film set, who made room for play, curiosity and mischief, and who taught me more than I think he ever realised. I will carry my admiration for him, and my gratitude for the time I was lucky enough to spend in his company, for the rest of my life.

Harriet Walter: ‘He enjoyed fame in the best possible way’ A memory: Patrick, wearing a team baseball cap to disguise the inimitable sculpture of his head, moving anonymously through the crowds at an American Football match in Michigan. Later during halftime he stepped up to the podium, bald pate boldly exposed, to conduct the University of Michigan Marching Band in a medley of TV theme tunes. I’ve never seen anyone so ecstatic. Fame came relatively late to Patrick and it was therefore enjoyed in the best possible way.

Later that night we performed together in Antony and Cleopatra. He was still buzzing. But then he was always alive in the moment and taught me that the sexual chemistry between the famous pair was more to do with their minds and their verbal sparring than in any fantastic costumes or scenery. His curiosity and courage earned him a full eventful and rewarding life. I was blessed in knowing him.

enrich.title_zh: 达芙妮·基恩与哈丽雅特·沃尔特谈与帕特里克·斯图尔特的合作：“我从没见过谁那么兴奋”
enrich.summary_zh: 本文是两位演员对帕特里克·斯图尔特的追忆。达芙妮·基恩回忆11岁拍《金刚狼3》时，这位前辈如何以温暖、幽默和约定“偷偷打个喷嚏”的顽皮，把片场这个陌生世界变成她的避风港；哈丽雅特·沃尔特则回忆他戴着棒球帽混在人群中、中场休息登台指挥乐队的狂喜时刻，认为他大器晚成，因此把名声享受得恰到好处。

paragraphs.en: Dafne Keen: ‘He asked me: have you noticed no-one ever sneezes in films?’ I had the unbelievable privilege of working with Patrick when I was 11 [in Logan]. He was a man of extraordinary warmth, wit and generosity. He possessed that increasingly rare ability to make everyone around him feel as though they were being let in on something wonderful. To work alongside him was to be reminded, every day, of what it means to love what you do, and to share that love with others. He imparted lessons in a way that was so wise, you didn’t even realise you were being taught.
paragraphs.zh: 达芙妮·基恩：“他问我：你注意到电影里从来没人打喷嚏吗？”我11岁那年（拍《金刚狼3》）有幸与帕特里克合作，那是难以想象的殊荣。他是个格外温暖、风趣、慷慨的人。他身上有一种如今越来越少见的能力：让身边每个人都觉得自己被拉进了一件美妙的事情里。与他共事，就是每天都被人提醒一次：热爱自己做的事、并把这份热爱分享给别人，究竟意味着什么。他传授道理的方式极为高明，你甚至没意识到自己正在被教导。

paragraphs.en: To describe Patrick simply as a remarkable man would feel an injustice to the sheer breadth of what made him so. He was a master of his craft, certainly, but also a teacher, a raconteur, a mischief-maker and, above all, a profoundly generous human being. He carried his knowledge lightly, his humour generously, and his affection for the people around him with a warmth that was impossible to miss.
paragraphs.zh: 只用“一个了不起的人”来形容帕特里克，对他之所以了不起的那份广博而言，反倒是一种亏欠。他当然是本行的大家，但同时也是老师、讲故事的高手、爱搞恶作剧的人，而最重要的是，一个极其慷慨的人。他的学问举重若轻，他的幽默毫不吝惜，他对身边人的情意带着一种让人无法忽视的温度。

paragraphs.en: He had a seemingly inexhaustible supply of jokes that could make the longest, most arduous days on set pass in minutes. I remember walking around one of the house sets with him and remarking that the only thing missing from the home was a dog. Without missing a beat, Patrick began barking and behaving like one, until I was absolutely roaring with laughter. It was that sort of instinctive silliness, a complete willingness to abandon any notion of grandeur or self-importance, that made being around him such a joy.
paragraphs.zh: 他的笑话似乎取之不尽，能让片场最漫长、最辛苦的日子几分钟就过去。我记得有一次和他一起在一处室内布景里走动，我说这个家里唯一缺的就是一条狗。帕特里克毫不犹豫，立刻学起狗叫、装起狗来，直到我笑得前仰后合。正是这种本能的傻气，这种完全愿意抛开任何架子与自我重要感的态度，让待在他身边成了一件那么快乐的事。

paragraphs.en: He was equally gifted at talking to children and professors alike, shifting his linguistic code to meet whoever happened to be in front of him. I remember the little snippets of Shakespeare, Ibsen, Chekhov and Pinter he would spontaneously grace us with, sharing passages from the works he loved as though letting us in on a private little world. He could move from the most sophisticated literary conversation to the most ridiculous schoolyard mischief without ever seeming to change gear.
paragraphs.zh: 他和孩子、和教授都同样聊得来，会根据面前站着的是谁而随时切换自己的语言方式。我记得他会即兴赏我们几段莎士比亚、易卜生、契诃夫和品特，把所爱作品里的段落分享出来，仿佛在让我们走进一个私密的小世界。他能从最高深的文学讨论，一转而进入最幼稚的校园恶作剧，而且看上去完全不用“换挡”。

paragraphs.en: Patrick was an incredibly protective scene partner and colleague. He had a way of making you feel included, listened to and respected, even when you were just a clueless 11-year-old finding your feet in the pressure-filled adult world of a film set. I remember him noticing me looking longingly at his Professor X wheelchair, and secretly approaching me to explain that if you pushed the stick hard enough, it went very, very fast. He then proceeded to invite me on it, encouraging me to go faster. I remember him hatching little plans with me, things we could sneak into scenes to make the set feel more like a playground and less like the intimidating grown-up world it could sometimes be.
paragraphs.zh: 帕特里克是那种极其护着搭档的演员和同事。他总有办法让你觉得自己被接纳、被倾听、被尊重，哪怕你只是个一无所知的11岁小孩，正在那个压力重重、成人主导的电影片场里摸索着站稳脚跟。我记得他注意到我眼巴巴地盯着他那把X教授的轮椅，就悄悄走过来告诉我：只要把操纵杆推得够狠，它能跑得非常非常快。接着他就请我坐上去，还鼓励我开快点。我记得他和我一起偷偷琢磨些小计划，想些什么能塞进镜头里的小动作，让片场更像游乐场，而不像它有时那样令人生畏的成人世界。

paragraphs.en: On one of our first days together, after an incredibly intense take, he turned to me and asked, entirely seriously, “Have you ever noticed, no one ever sneezes in films?” I stared at him for a moment before agreeing that he was quite right. “We should try to sneeze in this one,” he said. And so we made a pact to try to sneak a sneeze into a take. It was such a Patrick observation: at once completely absurd and rather brilliant. He was an artist with an extraordinary attentiveness to the world around him, someone who noticed the smallest details and understood that there was always something worth questioning, even in the most familiar conventions of his craft.
paragraphs.zh: 我们合作的最初几天里，有一条拍得极其紧绷的镜头结束后，他转过身来，非常认真地问我：“你有没有注意到，电影里从来没人打喷嚏？”我盯着他看了一会儿，然后承认他说得很对。“这一部我们得试着打个喷嚏。”他说。于是我们约定好，要设法在某一条里偷偷加进一个喷嚏。这个观察太“帕特里克”了：既完全荒诞，又相当精妙。他是那种对周遭世界有着非凡专注力的艺术家，会注意到最细微的地方，也懂得总有些东西值得追问——哪怕是在他这一行最习以为常的惯例里。

paragraphs.en: That was perhaps one of the loveliest things about him. He never seemed to outgrow the joy of playing, or to lose sight of the fact that, at its heart, acting should be fun. He had this extraordinary ability to make you feel that you weren’t simply there to do a job, but to be part of something, to contribute, to experiment and, above all, to enjoy yourself.
paragraphs.zh: 这也许是他身上最可爱的地方之一。他似乎从未“长大”到失去玩耍的快乐，也从未忘记：演戏的核心本该是好玩。他有一种了不起的能力，让你觉得自己不只是来干一份活儿，而是参与某件事情、有所贡献、可以去试验，而最重要的是——玩得开心。

paragraphs.en: There is something incredibly moving about the idea that an actor of his stature never made a child feel small, inexperienced or peripheral. He let you in on the secret. He made you feel like a fellow conspirator, a teammate.
paragraphs.zh: 一个像他这样有地位的演员，从没让一个孩子觉得自己渺小、没经验、无关紧要——想到这一点，格外让人动容。他把你拉进了那个秘密里。他让你觉得自己是同谋，是队友。

paragraphs.en: I learnt so much from him. He was, however briefly, my colleague and my acting professor, and he will forever be my Professor X. Someone who built a little safe haven for me on the often alien world of a film set, who made room for play, curiosity and mischief, and who taught me more than I think he ever realised. I will carry my admiration for him, and my gratitude for the time I was lucky enough to spend in his company, for the rest of my life.
paragraphs.zh: 我从他身上学到了太多。他曾是我的同事、我的表演老师，无论时间多短暂；而他将永远是我的X教授。他在片场这个常常显得陌生的世界里，为我搭起一个小小的避风港，为玩耍、好奇与恶作剧留出空间，教给我的东西，我想比他意识到的还要多。我将带着对他的敬仰，以及对我有幸与他共度那段时光的感激，度过我的余生。

paragraphs.en: Harriet Walter: ‘He enjoyed fame in the best possible way’ A memory: Patrick, wearing a team baseball cap to disguise the inimitable sculpture of his head, moving anonymously through the crowds at an American Football match in Michigan. Later during halftime he stepped up to the podium, bald pate boldly exposed, to conduct the University of Michigan Marching Band in a medley of TV theme tunes. I’ve never seen anyone so ecstatic. Fame came relatively late to Patrick and it was therefore enjoyed in the best possible way.
paragraphs.zh: 哈丽雅特·沃尔特：“他以最好的方式享受了名声” 一段回忆：帕特里克戴着球队的棒球帽，遮住他那无可复制的“头部雕塑”，在密歇根一场美式橄榄球比赛的人群里不被人认出地穿行。后来在中场休息时，他走上指挥台，光头大胆地露了出来，指挥密歇根大学行进乐队演奏了一组电视主题曲串烧。我从没见过谁那么兴奋。名声来得相对较晚，因此他也以最好的方式享受了它。

paragraphs.en: Later that night we performed together in Antony and Cleopatra. He was still buzzing. But then he was always alive in the moment and taught me that the sexual chemistry between the famous pair was more to do with their minds and their verbal sparring than in any fantastic costumes or scenery. His curiosity and courage earned him a full eventful and rewarding life. I was blessed in knowing him.
paragraphs.zh: 那天晚上，我们又同台演出了《安东尼与克莉奥佩特拉》。他仍然兴奋不已。不过他向来都是活在当下的，也是他让我明白：这对著名情侣之间的性张力，更多来自他们的头脑与言辞交锋，而不是任何华丽的服装或布景。他的好奇心与勇气，为他赢得了充实、跌宕而富有收获的一生。能认识他，是我的福气。

vocab.meaning_zh: 善于讲故事的人，健谈者（书面语，常用于人物特写）
vocab.example_en: He was a gifted raconteur who could hold a dinner table spellbound for hours.
vocab.example_zh: 他是个讲故事的能手，能让一桌人如痴如醉地听上好几个小时。

vocab.meaning_zh: 毫不犹豫地，不假思索地（原指乐队不间断地跟住节拍）
vocab.example_en: I asked him why he was late, and without missing a beat he said, ‘I was rescuing a cat.’
vocab.example_zh: 我问他为什么迟到，他眼都不眨地说：“我在救一只猫。”

vocab.meaning_zh: （悄悄地）策划、酝酿（计划、主意），常与 plan/scheme 搭配
vocab.example_en: The two of them hatched a plan to surprise the director on his birthday.
vocab.example_zh: 两人悄悄策划了一个在导演生日当天给他惊喜的计划。

vocab.meaning_zh: 长大而不再需要、失去（某种兴趣、习惯）；此处指“告别玩耍的快乐”
vocab.example_en: He never outgrew his boyish enthusiasm for trains.
vocab.example_zh: 他对火车的那种孩子气的热情，一辈子都没消退。

vocab.meaning_zh: 边缘的、无足轻重的；此处形容“让人觉得被晾在一边”
vocab.example_en: Children hate feeling peripheral when adults are talking.
vocab.example_zh: 大人在说话时，孩子最讨厌自己被晾在一边。

vocab.meaning_zh: （专业或道德上的）声望、地位，不指身高
vocab.example_en: She is an artist of international stature.
vocab.example_zh: 她是一位具有国际声望的艺术家。

vocab.meaning_zh: 言语交锋、你来我往的斗嘴（spar 原指拳击中的试探性出拳）
vocab.example_en: Their friendship was built on years of affectionate verbal sparring.
vocab.example_zh: 他们的友谊建立在多年既亲密又针锋相对的斗嘴之上。

vocab.meaning_zh: 欣喜若狂的，极度兴奋的
vocab.example_en: The crowd was ecstatic when the band came back for an encore.
vocab.example_zh: 乐队返场时，人群欣喜若狂。

vocab.meaning_zh: 换挡；比喻（话题、状态）突然切换到另一种模式
vocab.example_en: She can change gear from small talk to hard bargaining in a second.
vocab.example_zh: 她能从闲聊一秒切换到强硬的讨价还价。

sentences.en: It was that sort of instinctive silliness, a complete willingness to abandon any notion of grandeur or self-importance, that made being around him such a joy.
sentences.structure: 主干：It was … that made being around him such a joy（强调句，被强调部分是主语 that sort of instinctive silliness）；a complete willingness … self-importance 是同位语，解释前面的 silliness；动名词短语 being around him 作 made 的宾语。
sentences.analysis_zh: 作者用 It was X that … 的强调句型，把“那种本能的傻气”提到句子重音位置，而不是平铺直叙“待在他身边很快乐，因为他很傻”。中间的逗号同位语把抽象的 silliness 具体化为“彻底放下身段”，让读者先看到态度再看到结论。写作上值得学的是：先给评价性名词（silliness、joy），再补同位语解释，语气亲切不失分量。

sentences.en: Someone who built a little safe haven for me on the often alien world of a film set, who made room for play, curiosity and mischief, and who taught me more than I think he ever realised.
sentences.structure: 这是一个省略了主句的名词性片段（承接上句 my Professor X 作同位语）；Someone 后接三个并列的 who 定语从句：built … / made room for … / taught me …；more than I think he ever realised 是比较从句，I think 为插入成分。
sentences.analysis_zh: 整句没有谓语主句，靠三个 who 从句平行铺开，是悼念文字常见的“叠加式”句法：情绪浓到不作完整陈述，只把定语一层层挂上去。三个动词 built / made room / taught 由具体（避风港）到抽象（教导），层层递进；结尾 more than I think he ever realised（他大概都没意识到）用低调陈述表达最高评价，是英文悼文里典型的克制笔法。

sentences.en: But then he was always alive in the moment and taught me that the sexual chemistry between the famous pair was more to do with their minds and their verbal sparring than in any fantastic costumes or scenery.
sentences.structure: 主干：he was … and taught me that …；that 引导宾语从句，从句内是 more to do with A than (with) B 的比较结构；But then 是口语化的转折连接语，意为“不过话说回来”。
sentences.analysis_zh: more to do with A than B 是外刊高频比较框架，意为“与其说取决于 B，不如说取决于 A”，注意 than 后可省略介词，形成 A 与 B 的不完全对称（to do with / in），这在口语化书面语里很常见。But then 不是“但是那时”，而是用来轻轻补充理由的“不过嘛”，把上一句的“他还兴奋着”接到人物性格上：他向来活在当下。

background.title: 帕特里克·斯图尔特：X教授与“大器晚成”的名声
background.text_zh: 帕特里克·斯图尔特是英国资深舞台演员，长期出演皇家莎士比亚剧团剧目；大众最熟悉他的两个角色，是《星际迷航：下一代》中的皮卡德舰长和《X战警》系列中的X教授（Charles Xavier）。达芙妮·基恩提到的《金刚狼3》（Logan, 2017）中，他与休·杰克曼、当时11岁的基恩（饰劳拉／X-23）同片演出。斯图尔特在《星际迷航》走红时已年过四十，所以沃尔特说他的名声“来得相对较晚”，也因此能从容对待——这正是文中那句“以最好的方式享受名声”的含义，也解释了为何两位女演员都在用过去时说“他曾是”。

background.title: 美式橄榄球中场秀与大学行进乐队
background.text_zh: 美国大学橄榄球比赛的中场休息（halftime）通常由本校行进乐队（marching band）上场表演，规模可达数百人，是校园传统和观众期待的一部分；密歇根大学的行进乐队尤为著名。指挥这样一支乐队上场，需要在台上大幅挥动双臂，对一位以“光头”形象著称的演员来说，摘下帽子登台本身就是一种放下架子的姿态。文中“戴棒球帽混在人群里”与“光头大胆露出指挥乐队”构成对照，写的是名气与自在之间的分寸感。

title_en: D.C. and Virginia Join the Fight to Block Trump’s Triumphal Arch. What Happens Next?
